recipes.name: Homemade Deviled Ham Sandwiches
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound cooked ham, cut into chunks
3 tablespoons low-fat creamy salad dressing (such as Miracle Whip Light®)
1 dash hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®), or to taste

steps.text: Process ham and onion in a food processor until very finely chopped.
Transfer ham mixture to a bowl. Thoroughly mix in salad dressing, honey, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, mustard powder, paprika, salt, white pepper, and hot pepper sauce.
Make sandwiches by spreading a generous layer deviled ham between 2 slices bread, or cover and refrigerate deviled ham until ready to make sandwiches.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Deviled Ham Sandwiches
raw_recipe.description: A generous layer of this homemade deviled ham spread onto thinly sliced bread with mayonnaise and butter pickles makes a delicious lunch sandwich.

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe exact, only using reduced fat Hellman's mayonnaise as we don't use Miracle Whip. I also didn't have Tabasco, I used a good dash of Frank's Hot Sauce. We ate up every little bit of this. Honestly, this reminds me of my childhood. My Grandma used to make me bologna/ham spread regularly--it's total comfort food for me and now it is for my husband and kids. I served garlic dills on the side but next time, I think I'll throw them into the food processor with the ham and onion.

I made this today from leftover Easter ham. Honey Baked Ham. I did not have salad dressing, only mayonnaise. I added about 1/4 cup of white vinegar and a tablespoon of sugar. I left out the tabasco because family members will not eat spicy foods. 
This turned out incredibly delicious. I could eat this all by itself. My 80 year old mother-in-law ate every bite of her sandwich and we have problems getting her to eat! We will no longer eat store bought devilled ham. Love this recipe!

Oh my goodness, this was incredible! I had some leftover peach glazed ham (recipe on AR) in the freezer. I figured I’ll just give this recipe a try and I’m so glad I did. I omitted the honey as the ham already had a sweet element to it. I added a couple of spicy pickles and extra dashes of hot sauce (I used Valentina). The sweet, salty, and spicy combination was spot on. One thing I would recommend in addition to the pickles is to use purple onion instead of yellow or white. It’s the perfect flavor to correspond with the spicy ingredients. Thank you, BL, for this extremely delicious recipe!

Update, 11/21/19: Hi folks, BL here. I was looking for a holiday recipe & ran across this & paused to read new reviews. I always get a thrill reading your comments; thank you to all who tried it & took the time to leave a review. You made my day! 
PLEASE NOTE: I found that my “original” submitted recipe is still in my saved box & noticed that the “published“ version omitted my note that *1/4 onion* was about *2 Tablespoons*!!!! Obviously 1/4 of a large onion would be MUCH MORE so I suggest using 2 T chopped onion, or to taste. If I could update the published version I would! Also ham can vary a great deal between salty & sweet, so please consider the type of ham if you try this & adjust the salt/honey/spice accordingly. I created this with a slightly sweet leftover spiral holiday ham (Sam’s) & it needed a pinch of salt. For a salty ham add an extra 1/2-1 tsp honey & omit the salt. 

I really was *trying* to copycat a certain “deviled honey ham spread” we used to take on camping trips & it seemed pretty close (actually I think it’s better). Texans tens to like like a bit of spice & zip so this recipe has both. Leave out the Tabasco and/or dry mustard for a milder version. We have only ever eaten this on sandwich bread with a thin coat of mayo & a thick layer of bread & butter pickles; that is one amazing sandwich! If I were making it for crackers I would definitely add pickles or even relish; pickles are a MUST imo. It works well with deli turkey or ham too, but leftover holid
Great! This is what you do with Thanksgiving, Christmas, or Easter leftover ham. I also added 3 Tablespoons of dill pickle relish... So Yummy!

I am going to take liberty with my stars. I forgot the Worcestershire sauce, used a dejon mustard in loo of yellow-dry, and took Sarah Jo's suggestion and ground the pickles with the ham n onions. Ssooo yummy!! I did add green onion for some color. I accidentally ground it up a bit too much. The hot sauce will be added to the top! Thank you BL! Keeper and Perfect for the up coming entertainment season. A pretty bowl, great crackers and you've got a start to a Rockin party!!
Made this last night with leftover Thanksgiving ham. It was very good!

This is the first time i have made a ham spread. I used brown mustard, green onions, black pepper and cyanne pepper because It was what I had. I don't even like ham that much and this recipe was so great I ate two sandwiches with tomato and swiss cheese. I had to keep myself from eating it all. The cyanne really gave it a kick! I also used Naturally Fresh Classic Ceaser Salad dressing and I think it really added a nice flavor.

This was way too sweet for my liking. After reading several reviews I remembered the ham I used had been originally cooked all day in a crock pot with mustard & brown sugar. Therefore my experiment today tastes like honey ham. It's good, but I was hoping to get the original flavor of Underwood deviled ham with the white label. Not even close. Next time if I use leftover brown.sugar ham I'll have to omit the honey/agave.
I have made this with both leftover ham and roast beef. It's delicious both ways.

I was never a big fan of deviled ham but rather than throw away some ham that needed used, I ran across this recipe and gave it a try. Followed it exactly and have to say it's delicious! I liked it so much, I used the ingredients with some chicken I wanted to use up also. It was just as good with the addition of a little more Miracle Whip. Took me back to my childhood! Will definitely make both again.
Loved it. I never thought of using honey

I have never eaten deviled ham that wasn't from that little tin can with the paper wrapper and was expecting something similar in flavor with a much better, less loose, more meaty texture. The texture on this is great. This was simple to put together. I just used a cutting board and good knife to mince the ham and onions up. I cut back on the onion because onions are strong and bitter to me, but still wanted to keep this as close to written as possible. I used mayonnaise instead of salad dressing. I didn't like the flavor at all and found it to be bitter, oniony, sharp, and overall unappealing. I did take two bites to make sure. I was not able to finish this as it was not at all like the canned deviled ham in flavor and was too sharp, too strong, and too much. I am not sure which ingredient to tweak as many of them bring that sharp bold bite. Sorry this just wasn't for me, although it seems to be a decent recipe.
Very good. Made it as written. Makes great sandwiches.
This is a very good starter recipe. I added extra salad dressing, worcestshire, prepared mustard and hot sauce to meet my families taste.
Great recipe BL. So yummy. I followed your recipe except substituted Hellmann Mayo for miracle whip, and I cut honey to one teaspoon as I prefer less sweetness. Great for leftover ham.
I made it just like written, didn't taste like deviled ham, tasted like regular ham salad.

This recipe turned out great. I actually didn't really follow the recipe. I added ingredients that I had at the time and it was very good. very easy to make. It is now on my must make recipe box when I have extra ham.

I made this to help use up leftover ham. The family liked this recipe. I went by the recipe as best I could except I didn't add any hot sauce and I had to use a substitute for the honey. I do think I will not add any salt the next time I make it as it is on the salty side but not enough for me to scrap. I tried this on triscuits first and didn't seem to like it, but when I tried on ritz crackers I liked it better. The next day I made a sandwich and liked it even more, so if you aren't sure about it at first try it on or in something else. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
This recipe is ok but there really are too many ingredients. The second time I made it, I added celery, deleted the honey and the mustard and would add a star to the rating with those changes.
